title: Kat Cosgrove
_source: Fan GMV 'I Need a Hero - Destiny 2: Lightfall' (det0BbS_9GU, channel Kahiyao), VP9 1920x1080p60 bt709, format 303. Staged at ~/Videos/wolves-kat/sources/. Third-party copyrighted, same provenance question acts II and VI carry (#55). Footage is never committed.

trim._note: One hard cut, no dissolve. Content starts at 0 (only a ~0.1s black fade-in lead, not a bumper -- verified from opening frames). Clip time == source time, so every window below is both.

letterbox._note: 2.40:1, MEASURED for this source: cropdetect limit=24 gives crop=1920:800:0:140, and a per-region signalstats pass confirms the top and bottom 140px bands are pure video-black (YAVG ~16.1). Dialogue plates seat INSIDE the bottom matte and never cover the picture.

reveal._note: The nameplate, on the hero shot. 6.03-12.60 is ONE continuous shot (a slow push-in verified by a scene-detect pass at threshold 0.25 finding no cut), so the framing change across the hold is camera movement, not an edit. Card geometry reveal.html left:4%, bottom:392px -- the 392 is load-bearing: Kat's card carries a populated class row ('Sentinel Titan') the earlier Sabot-6 card omitted, making it 129px taller in render space, and the inherited bottom:520px pushed the card top onto the prone Guardian's jaw at ~25.3-25.8s.
reveal._not_repo_rendered: The nameplate card is NOT rendered from this record. It was screenshotted from ~/Videos/wolves-kat/render/reveal.html, and its copy is Kat's authored Guardian identity, which is reproduced verbatim from the website's characters.json and never written here. build_kat.py therefore consumes the existing PNG from the project folder rather than re-rendering it: the dialogue is the thing that had no home (#118), and inventing a nameplate row to close a smaller gap would be exactly the failure the copy rules forbid. Giving the reveal a repo-rendered card is separate work.

bed.track: dArtagnan - Holding out for a Hero
bed._note: The GMV's own audio is DROPPED and replaced, at the owner's request; justified because the source audio is a wide stereo music mix (side/mid 0.53, L/R correlation 0.56), not an isolated effects layer worth preserving. The window was chosen by LOCAL TRANSCRIPTION (faster-whisper, word-level) mapping every gendered reference onto the timeline: Kat is a she and the song calls its hero 'he' throughout the choruses, so the bed must avoid those lines. 134.6757-168.6757 is the ONLY fully gender-neutral 34.0s window in the entire song, verified twice -- the base model flagged a false positive and a re-run with the `small` model confirmed the zone is clean, the next chorus's first 'He's' starting 0.08s AFTER the cut and landing under the fade-out. A transcription of the rendered bed reports zero gendered tokens. Start 134.6757 is an exact beat inside an instrumental gap, and the window is natively exactly 34.0s, so there is no atempo at all. Level is a FIXED -1.0 dB trim for headroom, deliberately not limited or dynamics-processed.
bed._usage_class: third_party_copyrighted -- see #55 and the rights section of AGENTS.md. Not committed here; staged in ~/Videos/wolves-kat/sources/.

delivered._note: THIS is what ~/Videos/Wolves/Prod/04-kat.mp4 hardlinks to: FLAC stereo, measured 1829850 bit/s. Note that render/run-kat.sh's own DEFAULTS build the OTHER file (AAC 5.1) -- the delivered master is the ACODEC=flac SURROUND=0 variant. scripts/build_kat.py defaults to what is actually delivered, so a rebuild cannot silently swap the two.

variant_51._note: The 5.1 sibling, NOT delivered. The artist's stereo mix passes through bit-exact as FL/FR; the only added channel is LFE, derived additively. FC/BL/BR are digital silence -- no upmix, no EQ, no loudness processing. ffmpeg's `surround` filter is deliberately not used: it resynthesises the soundfield (front channels correlate only ~0.96 with the original) and adds ~43 ms of latency, which desyncs audio from picture. LFE_GAIN compensates the standard +10 dB LFE playback gain applied by receivers.

encode._loop_framerate_note: run-kat.sh passed `-framerate 60` on every still input. Act V did not, and its master was built that way, so whether to pass it is recorded per act rather than assumed.

unresolved: The three radio voices krook, jeefy and mrbobbytables spoke ONLY placeholder copy and were dropped; their avatars remain on disk in ~/Videos/wolves-kat/render/ so the previous cut stays reproducible, but they are not in this record.

`ian`, `tabbysable` and `cailyn-codes` are NOT bound in vocab/casting.yaml; their round is RETIRED (see `retired`) so nothing on screen depends on them now, but the words stay theirs if restored -- binding remains #26's territory.

Avatars are NOT committed (they are people's photographs, and this repo commits no binaries of that kind). scripts/build_kat.py reads them from the project folder and reports which are missing rather than substituting anything.

#118's remaining Kat-section beats are still held: '27 Kubernetes releases' / '6 KubeCons' (overlay captions with unsettled clock, #109), [lindsey] and [christoph] (unresolved bindings), and 'You're wearing a dress' (depends on the christoph exchange).

p3c-hey ('HEY! We know when you're not upstreaming!') has NO NAMED SPEAKER -- the owner's instruction gave the words only. It ships as the uncast TBD speaker with the drawn crest; naming the voice is one owner word and a rebuild.
_plate_kind: Every dialogue plate is `kind: chat` -- tools/plate.py's port of the wolves plate.html pill, which is THIS REPO'S renderer for it. The delivered master's plates were screenshotted from plate.html itself by playwright in ~/Videos/wolves-kat/render/; a rebuild from this manifest re-renders them with plate.py instead. The two are the same design and the port is tested (tests/test_plate.py), but they are not guaranteed pixel-identical, so a rebuild is compared before it is delivered rather than assumed to match.
_timing: `at` + `dur` are tools/plate.py's own manifest fields, so this file renders with `plate.py render --manifest` unmodified. `fade_out_at` is absolute film time, matching the ffmpeg `fade=t=out:st=` it generates.
